newsitem.title: GREECE: FX FORWARDS FIRM ON U-TURN IN LATE DEALINGS.
newsitem.headline: FX FORWARDS FIRM ON U-TURN IN LATE DEALINGS.

text.p: Greek depos were little changed but forex forwards in short periods reversed course trading higher in late trade discounting a liquidity squeeze due to forex outflows and funding for FRNs and bonds next week, dealers said.

"We have had a volatile day," said a trader at a foreign bank. "Depos are steady but forex forwards have firmed after today's fixing outflows and expected funding for FRNs and bonds to be auctioned next week that will squeeze liquidity."

Greece will auction about 200 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs with the first coupon at 13.40 percent with the 12-month T-bill rate set at 12 percent and the spread at 10 basis points on November 22, the finance ministry said in a statement.

It will also auction 100 billion drachmas of three-year, 11 percent coupon bonds on November 12. Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said this week that a five-year bond would be auctioned but the ministry appears to have changed its mind and substituted the three-year bond.
Banks sold about 200 million ecus for drachmas at today's fixing and ecu/drachma penetrated the 303 level trading around 303.10 in late dealings.
"This will affect liquidity next week and has ahd an impact on rates," said a dealer.
The central bank came out on both sides in its daily overnight intervention injecting cash at 13.40 percent and draining money at 12.40 percent.
"The market remains short overall. The central bank was mostly on the offer side," said another dealer.
The mark was quoted at 157.73/83 drachmas from Friday's 157.950 fix, the dollar at 237.84/94 drachmas from 237.940 and the Ecu at 302.77/87 from 303.080 drachmas.
